storage_extensions.usage: At query start: resolve 'Japan' -> japan_code and 'USA' -> usa_code via linear scan of dict.offsets+dict.data (19351 entries, ~150KB, one-time). In CSR scan, after the Y[mv] year-bitset check, test code = mi_info_prefix[r]: if code != japan_code && code != usa_code, skip — this avoids reading mi_info.off and mi_info.dat (118MB + 626MB) for ~60-70% of year-passing rows that don't start with 'Japan:' or 'USA:'. For survivors, still run the existing mi_info_match (memmem '200' in the remainder) to enforce the full LIKE semantics (Japan:%200% / USA:%200%). codes.bin is 29MB; strided access in CSR order is bandwidth-friendly. If japan_code or usa_code resolves to a value not present in the dict (0), skip the corresponding pattern.

like_strategies.method: Step 1: resolve 'Japan' and 'USA' to uint16 codes via prefix_dict (one-time linear scan of ~19351 dict entries). Step 2: in CSR scan, after Y[mv] passes, test prefix_codes[r] ∈ {japan_code, usa_code} (single uint16 compare, no varlen read). Step 3: for survivors, read mi_info bytes and run memmem('200', tail) on the suffix after the prefix to enforce the '%200%' part. If japan_code or usa_code resolves to 0 (not present in dict), skip that branch.

scan_mi_csr_filter_order: 3. test Y bitset at mv — if NOT set, continue (skips ALL subsequent reads)
4. code = mi_info_prefix_codes[r]; if code != japan_code && code != usa_code: continue (skips varlen offset+data reads)
5. read mi_info_off[r], mi_info_off[r+1] and the suffix after the prefix length
6. require memmem('200', 3) in the suffix portion
main_scan_filter_order: 1. mc range walk: require any cn_country_code[company_id-1]==cc_us; break on first hit
2. ci range walk: require role_id==rt_actress (cheap int compare)
4. pid = ci.person_id; require P_and_an bit set (single L2-resident bit test)
5. require ci.note voice-set (varlen, only for rare survivors)
6. update local MIN(name) and (once per movie) MIN(title)
optimization_notes: Iter 1 reduced total 68->66ms but scan_mi_csr_year_first_then_like still dominates at 24ms (36% of total). Diagnosis: after Y bitset prunes ~50% of release_dates rows, the remaining ~4M rows still do random varlen reads into mi_info.off (118MB) and mi_info.dat (626MB) — both vastly exceeding L3 (12MB). Only ~30-40% of these rows actually start with 'Japan:' or 'USA:', so 60-70% of varlen reads are wasted. Strategy: Category E (storage extension). Built column_versions/movie_info.info.prefix_dict — a uint16 dict-encoded column where each mi row's code is the dict id of its letter-only prefix-before-colon (or 0 if no usable prefix). At query time, resolve 'Japan' and 'USA' to codes once, then in the CSR scan check prefix_codes[r] ∈ {japan_code, usa_code} BEFORE reading info.off/info.dat. The codes column is 29MB strided-sequential in CSR order, far cheaper than random probes into 744MB of varlen data. Expected: scan_mi drops from 24ms to ~10-13ms. All other phases (build_Y, build_P, main_scan) unchanged. Year threshold 2000 preserved verbatim.
